summary: RUNTIME SEMANTICS, not a compiler bug. Four-mode replay: default ABORTS (49 flips, 107.23s), SPU_SHADOW=1 ABORTS identically with 0 divergences (39 flips, 82.42s), SPU_NO_AOT=1 ABORTS identically at 102.59s once the window is long enough (the 110s run had only just cleared the 107s abort), SPU_STRICT=1 dies at 0.319s on lsa 0x818 (the SPURS kernel entry). There is nothing compiled to blame: out-rdr/spu/spu_registry.cpp is 'count=0; return nullptr;' and the linked symbol disassembles to movq $0x0,(%rdi); xor; ret, so aot::index().active is false in every mode. The named block: on SecondaryCellSpursKernel0, two MFC GETs (cmd 0x40, 128 bytes) from EA 0x00000000 into LSA 0x1a100 at pc 0x06428 and 0x06510; the runtime's unmapped-DMA fallback (thread.cpp:1041) zero-fills the destination over live SPURS kernel code (0x1a100 is rotqbyi r48,r49,8 in the normal path); the zero word decodes as 'stop 0x0'; stop_and_signal(0) has no case and returns false; the group stops with cause 2; libspurs asserts handler.c:198; _sys_process_exit(0x8001000c). Causal proof on the same binary: gating that zero-fill behind GOWA_SPU_DMA_NOZERO=1 removes the abort entirely (runs to 170s, no assertion), control reproduces it at 102.79s.

noaot_110s.note: window only just cleared the 107s abort

evidence.aot_table: empty (spu_registry.cpp 16 lines, compiled_blocks disassembles to movq $0x0,(%rdi); xor %eax,%eax; ret)
evidence.shadow_note: SPU_SHADOW is inert with an empty AOT table: verify_block only runs when a compiled block b exists (thread.cpp:1871), and shadow_checks/shadow_diffs stay 0; the SPU SHADOW end-of-run verdict never prints because the abort exits first. The shadow run therefore proves nothing about compiler/interpreter agreement.
evidence.caveat: GOWA_SPU_DMA_NOZERO=1 is a diagnostic probe gated by env, added only to establish causality; it is not proposed as the fix.
